cards.title: 2025 U.S. Property Claims Satisfaction Study (Claims Journal coverage)
cards.claim: Homeowner claim satisfaction falls steadily as repairs lengthen, with long-duration claims scoring far below those completed within about ten days.
cards.relevance: Gives an external threshold-style benchmark consistent with the dataset's 20-day split showing worse outcomes for slow claims.
cards.limit: US homeowners property claims; satisfaction, not renewal; 2025 redesign not comparable to prior years.

cards.title: 2025 U.S. Property Claims Satisfaction Study: ease of communication
cards.claim: Satisfaction is dramatically higher when customers find it easy to communicate with the insurer, with voicemails, repeat calls and slow follow-ups named as failure points.
cards.relevance: Suggests the complaint may be as much about communication during the wait as the wait itself, a testable lever.
cards.limit: Correlational, US property claims, same source page as RT-01.

cards.title: US property insurers lift claims satisfaction despite pricing headwinds
cards.claim: Faster repair and payment cycles helped insurers offset the negative effect of higher prices, while customers hit by premium increases plus high out-of-pocket costs were notably less satisfied.

stat.value: 702 overall; 606 for premium increase + deductible >= $1,000 group; repair 29.6 days, payment 40.7 days

cards.relevance: Shows speed and price interact; out-of-pocket cost can depress satisfaction independent of wait.
cards.limit: US homeowners, satisfaction not renewal; no switching figures reported.

cards.title: J.D. Power: despite cycle time decrease, premium increases erode trust and drive record shopping
cards.claim: Poor claim experiences are linked to departures, and claim-related rate increases cut satisfaction sharply, even as auto repair cycle times were falling.

stat.value: 80% of poor-claims-experience customers left or plan to leave; 100+ point drop after claim-related rate increase; cycle 22.3 days

cards.relevance: Links bad claim experience to attrition while showing the post-claim premium increase is a competing driver.
cards.limit: US auto; the 80% is stated intent plus actual, secondary reporting of J.D. Power.

cards.title: A poor claims experience can drive customers away
cards.geo: US data (12 P&C insurers), Netherlands-hosted page
cards.claim: Deloitte's analysis of about 4,000 P&C customer responses finds the claims process strongly influences future purchase yet earns the lowest positive sentiment, with slow processing and unclear status updates weakening it.

stat.what: Sample behind the claims-vs-purchase influence finding

cards.relevance: Names slow processing, unclear status and settlement delays as sentiment drags, matching the Head of Retention's complaints.
cards.limit: Publication year not stated on page; no renewal percentages extracted.

cards.title: How to improve customer retention in P&C insurance (snap chart)
cards.claim: Roughly half of customers satisfied with claims say they are likely to renew, versus about a third of those dissatisfied.
cards.relevance: Quantifies a renewal gap of the same order of magnitude as the 36% vs 16% non-renewal split.
cards.limit: Stated likelihood not behaviour; sample size and survey year not given (published Dec 2022, NPS Prism data).

cards.title: The case for retaining clients instead of finding new ones
cards.claim: An IBM Institute for Business Value expert told a Canadian insurance event that retaining a customer costs up to six times less than acquiring one.
cards.relevance: Provides a Canadian-published multiplier for sizing the value of saving slow-claim policyholders.
cards.limit: Cross-industry style rule of thumb, not personal-lines audited data; no Canadian retention rate given.

cards.title: J.D. Power: insurer claim behavior significantly influences renewal odds
cards.claim: Customers were least likely to renew when part of a claim was denied, and poor service made shopping far likelier than price frustration did.

stat.value: ~8x shopping likelihood for poor service vs ~5x for price frustration

cards.relevance: Shows claim outcome (denial) matters for renewal and that service ranks above price as a shopping trigger in that study.
cards.limit: 2020 US auto; no renewal percentages for denial; outcome vs speed not separated.

cards.title: LexisNexis: somewhat satisfied auto claimants often a flight risk
cards.claim: Claimants are only modestly more likely to shop than others, and even satisfied claimants shop, suggesting claim experience is one factor among several.

stat.value: 33% of claimants shopped/switched; 24% of very satisfied did; claimants 35% more likely to consider switching
stat.what: Switching after auto claim (n=1,409; 16.5M claim policies)

cards.relevance: Even very satisfied claimants shop at 24%, so satisfaction alone does not prevent churn; adjuster quality mattered more than speed.
cards.limit: US auto; speed not reported; vendor-sponsored.

cards.title: Claims delays drive one in four policyholders to switch insurer
cards.claim: A UK survey found one in four policyholders switched after a poor claims experience, with processing and settlement delays the leading complaints.
cards.relevance: Independent evidence that delay is the top named complaint behind claim-driven switching.
cards.limit: UK, self-reported, survey year not stated, small sample.

cards.title: Homeowners premium increases threaten customer loyalty (J.D. Power 2025)
cards.claim: Among homeowners who got a premium increase and are unlikely to renew, a large share name rising rates as the main reason.

stat.what: Of unlikely-to-renew customers with an increase citing rates as main reason

cards.relevance: Price-driven churn is real in renewal intent, a competing explanation to the claim-wait story.
cards.limit: US home, stated intent, sample not given; note the dataset shows no premium-quartile effect.

cards.title: 2026 J.D. Power property claims study as reposted by Insurance-Canada.ca
cards.claim: Digital tools drive satisfaction at each claim touchpoint, and satisfaction rose 20 points to 702 as repair and payment times shortened.
cards.relevance: Confirms the recent US benchmark for time to final payment and that digital updates correlate with satisfaction.
cards.limit: Contains no Canadian figures; US homeowners only.
